intentionalRegressions.reason: The vendored Java baseline rejects 'Vital signs' as the display for http://loinc.org#8716-3, which current tx.fhir.org $validate-code accepts (verified 2026-08-25 by direct $validate-code calls for all four codes this fixture's baseline errors on). Records follows the terminology server, so it does not reproduce that one error. It does reproduce the other three, which are genuine wrong-display errors the server also rejects: 11369-6, 30954-2 and 29762-2 with '<X> Narrative' forms. Configured against a terminology server the comparison therefore differs by exactly one Java-only error; without one Records has no LOINC designations at all and reproduces none of the four. An earlier version of this note claimed all four were intentionally not reproduced and attributed it to former Long Common Names being accepted; both parts were wrong.

Records reported the same v2-0203 PRN wrong-display finding twice for one element: the designation table emitted it as an error at the resource-qualified path, and the Bundle profile's own snapshot walk re-ran the code-system check inside the entry and emitted it again as a warning at the unqualified path. Removing the duplicate at the source (see isBundleEntryResourceDescendantPath in packages/validator/src/core/executors/terminology-executor-helpers.ts) leaves exactly the one row the Java baseline has, and changes exactly one row across the whole lane. The score falls 0.7214 -> 0.6972 because the duplicate was load-bearing for the similarity heuristic, not because coverage was lost: it made the warning count match Java exactly (22 vs 22 -> 21 vs 22, -0.020), and compareOutcomePaths prefix-matched it against the Java IdentifierType binding warning at entry.resource.identifier.type -- a warning Records does not emit at all (Java has three inside entries; Records has only the top-level Bundle.identifier.type one). Measured: additionally emitting those three true findings lowers the score further, to 0.668-0.680, because the warning count then misses by two. No version of making Records more correct keeps this case above 0.70 while the error gap (64 vs 68) stands; that gap is the real distance to parity here and is tracked separately. Holding the score by keeping a duplicate in customer output was rejected deliberately.
